subject: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment checklist and timeline
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna@cardiosync.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cardiosync.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff & POC environment checklist

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the routing/fallback capabilities. We want to move the evaluation forward and landed on a formal Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to unblock our security and procurement gates.

Attached is a rough MAP spreadsheet (CARDIOSYNC_MAP_v1.xlsx) that lists the items we need for a 3-week POC: org setup, API keys (eval + staging), IP allowlist entries, VPC peering, and a simple success criteria checklist. Our primary requirements are:
- Dedicated eval workspace (org) scoped to CardioSync test data
- Short-lived API keys for evaluation (30d) and a plan for rotation
- IP allowlist for our staging CIDR: 54.120.32.0/20
- VPC peering for higher-throughput tests (we can open a peering request once routing info is provided)

Can we confirm owners and a proposed timeline? Ideally we'd start provisioning this week and aim to run initial inference jobs by 06/10.

Thanks,
Anna Liu
Director of AI Engineering
CardioSync

Attachment: CARDIOSYNC_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna@cardiosync.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & POC environment checklist

Anna — thanks for the clear checklist and the MAP draft. We're aligned on the scope and can hit the 06/10 milestone with a focused runbook. Proposed owners and timeline below:

Owners / immediate actions
- Org & workspace provisioning: Vanessa Ortiz (me) — create CardioSync eval org and invite two engineers by 06/02
- API keys (evaluation & staging): Evelyn Hart — generate ephemeral eval keys and document rotation plan by 06/03
- Network (IP allowlist & VPC peering): Jordan Blake — provide peerable VPC info and allowlist ranges by 06/02
- Legal / procurement steps: CardioSync procurement (cc'd) to confirm PO/MSA cadence

Timeline (fast path)
- 06/02: Org created, initial API keys issued (ephemeral)
- 06/03: Network allowlist confirmed; peering request initiated
- 06/04–06/09: Warm-up tests, integration smoke tests
- 06/10: First throughput/latency run, evaluation checklist review

Two quick notes:
1) For the peering path, we suggest starting with a test VPC peering (limited subnet routes) before moving traffic to production networks. Jordan — can you outline the exact CIDR pairs and the minimal set of routes we need?
2) We'll upload an editable MAP in the shared Drive (link below) and drop a short canary prompt set for quality checks.

Doc links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_cardiosync-map
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4532

I'll follow up after Jordan and Evelyn chime in.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment stub: cardiosync-intro-onepager.pdf (referenced)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Anna Liu <anna@cardiosync.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & POC environment checklist

Anna / Vanessa — quick tech note on the peering/allowlist items. High-level plan:

1) IP allowlist
- Please add these outbound CIDRs to CardioSync staging allowlist: 52.24.160.0/20, 52.24.176.0/21
- If you have a NAT egress IP range, confirm exact IPs; we'll validate connectivity from our staging nodes.

2) VPC peering (test path)
- We recommend establishing a test peering with a limited route table: CardioSync staging subnet (54.120.32.0/20) <-> Redwood staging subnet (10.40.128.0/22)
- Peering prerequisites: a) routing entries to allow return path, b) security group rules permitting TCP 443 and ephemeral port ranges for VM management

3) Service account & service principal
- We'll create a service account for CardioSync with scoped access. For initial evaluation we can provide token-based auth; for long-term we'll provide a service principal and documented key rotation schedule.

4) Test keys and quotas
- Evelyn — please standby for a request to generate an ephemeral pair (eval/staging).

I'll attach a simplified network diagram (cardiosync-network-diagram.png) to this thread. If CardioSync's infra team prefers, we can run a 30-min network walkthrough on Wed 06/02 at 10:00 PT.

—Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: cardiosync-network-diagram.png (diagram stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Anna Liu <anna@cardiosync.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & POC environment checklist

Thanks — a couple operational points on API keys and org setup:

API keys
- We'll issue two types of keys: Ephemeral eval keys (30d, limited rate) and Staging keys (rotating every 14 days). Ephemeral keys will be restricted to the CardioSync eval org and to the endpoints used in the MAP.
- Rotation: we will provide a rotation runbook that automates creation and revocation via our console API. I'll deliver the runbook draft by 06/03.

Org setup
- I will create the CardioSync eval org and invite anna@cardiosync.com plus two engineers as admins. We'll pre-configure an IAM role with "inference-reader" and "inference-executor" scopes and restrict export permissions for the POC org.
- For auditing, Redwood will enable token-level logging for the eval org for the duration of the POC. If you need log export to your GCS/S3 bucket, share the bucket ARN and we'll add the sink.

Deliverables from Redwood
- Ephemeral eval keys (06/02)
- API rotation runbook (06/03)
- Access & audit config applied to eval org (06/02)

If CardioSync ops wants to test a sample requests set, send a brief curl that hits your expected staging endpoints and we'll validate NAT egress and TLS certs.

—Evelyn Hart
Platform Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: api-key-runbook-draft.docx (document stub)

From: Anna Liu <anna@cardiosync.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, procurement@cardiosync.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & POC environment checklist

Team — this looks great, and the fast path timeline works for us. Procurement will issue a short-form PO for the evaluation this afternoon; procurement@cardiosync.com will send the PO number once it's generated.

Confirmed items:
- 06/02: Org + ephemeral keys issued (we received the invite and initial key with limited scope)
- 06/02: Network walkthrough scheduled (thanks Jordan) — infra attended and validated allowlist CIDRs
- 06/03: Rotation runbook reviewed and accepted by our security lead
- 06/10: First evaluation run and pass/fail checklist review

We appreciate the audit logs being enabled. For the peering step, we'll start with the test peering and evaluate throughput before opening the production network.

Meeting: Let's lock a 30-min sync on Mon 06/07 at 09:00 PT to review warm-up results and any open blockers.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this on the road.

Best,
Anna Liu
Director of AI Engineering, CardioSync

Attachment: Signed-PO-stub.pdf (procurement placeholder)
